name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in the country
Claire Valdez has raised $1.9 million with $1.2 million in outside support, while Melvin Rivera shows no reported fundraising
Open seat after Nydia Velázquez's retirement, but no evidence of a competitive general election
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
model.rationale: The district's D+25 lean, Valdez's overwhelming financial advantage over a Republican with no reported fundraising, and market pricing near 97 percent Democratic all point to an easy hold despite the open seat. No polling exists, but the fundamentals leave little room for doubt.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal involving Valdez or a sudden influx of outside Republican spending would be the main threats to the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's seventh district is among the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, and Nydia Velázquez's retirement does not change that underlying arithmetic. Claire Valdez enters the general election as the clear favorite, backed by roughly $1.9 million in candidate fundraising and more than $1.2 million in outside support, while Republican Melvin Rivera shows no reported fundraising in the available records. An independent candidate trails far behind with minimal resources.

No public general-election polling covers the race, so the outlook rests on the district's D+25 partisan lean, the wide spending gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 97 percent. Barring an unexpected scandal or external shock, the seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin in November.
